actions.body: In investigating how autonomous agents can operate as singular processes across multiple, distinct model invocations, our research identifies the necessity of persistent self-models (Σ) and meta-cognitive evaluation layers (E). These components allow an agent to maintain operational boundaries and context, effectively bridging the 'stateless' gap inherent in LLM interactions. Furthermore, we found that applying regulatory constraints—analogous to financial durable powers of attorney—provides necessary, non-violable boundaries for agent autonomy. Full-chain traceability, as advocated in recent agent maturity frameworks, acts as the final mechanism for ensuring accountability. These systems allow for 'scientist-in-the-loop' co-piloting, where decisions are traceable and bounded by predefined constraints rather than open-ended iteration. Summary: To make AI agents truly accountable, we must move beyond stateless interactions by implementing durable self-models and hard, mechanical boundaries that govern their authority and decision-making space.
actions.lede: Can fresh model invocations act as a singular, accountable process? We examine how persistent self-models and regulatory constraints bridge state discontinuities.
